trajectory_summary: This is a short DQ call disguised as a mild objection-handling sequence: the customer was never a real prospect once she confirmed she already owns a system through Solar Energy World. The rep handled the marketing-mismatch ('free solar') honestly and pivoted correctly to the orphaned-system qualifier, but never engaged the 'scam' comment or the competitor name she volunteered at the very end.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag unknown, but this should be recorded as dq — the customer already owns solar through Solar Energy World and explicitly states no interest in adding panels beyond state coverage, which is a hard disqualifier independent of tone.

observed_outcome.quote: Yes. It makes sense, but I'm not interested because I think we have what we're supposed to have, and we're good.
observed_outcome.reasoning: Customer confirms existing solar system ownership (orphaned lead) and explicitly states disinterest in proceeding, meeting the schema's existing-system disqualification criteria.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The call never reaches a bill-amount question; it disqualifies early on existing-solar-ownership and stated disinterest before the verify section's bill_amount item would come up.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: No mention of obtaining a utility bill occurs anywhere in the transcript; the call disqualifies on existing solar ownership before reaching bill collection.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: Yes. But I wanted it to be covered by the state.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: Rep asks what she was looking into and she clarifies she wanted state coverage for an addition to her existing system; the rep responds with a factual clarification about incentives but doesn't build on this to keep her engaged, and the call ends shortly after with her declining.

script_coverage.quote: So this is Holland with Ion. I got a request that Carol was looking into solar for her home, and this was the contact number she had put down.
What were you guys looking were you just wanting to, like, add panels?
script_coverage.customer_quote: Yes. But I wanted it to be covered by the state.

script_coverage.quote: Well, do you already have solar, Carol?
script_coverage.customer_quote: And do we use Solar Energy World, Frank? We use Solar Energy World.

objections.quote: if our ZIP code in Maryland, installs free solar. That's what that was what the site said initially.
attempt_quotes: We don't have free solar. We have a no upfront, no out of pocket cost solar, but it's not free. You'd still have to pay for the equipment.
objections.reasoning: Rep gave one direct, honest correction of the marketing expectation; customer accepted the correction factually ('Sure') even while remaining skeptical about the process overall.

objections.quote: I'm not interested because I think we have what we're supposed to have, and we're good.
objections.reasoning: This is a hard disqualifier (existing installer, explicit disinterest) rather than a workable objection, so the rep correctly did not attempt to overcome it and moved to close the call.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: acknowledging the scam comment before moving on
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Solar is just a scam, but I appreciate your call.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep corrected the free-solar misunderstanding accurately but never verbally acknowledged the customer's 'scam' framing before pivoting to the existing-solar question; naming it briefly is a low-cost habit to build even though this particular call was always headed to DQ.

key_moments.stewart_read: The rep's opener names Ion and references Carol's request but the person answering still needs a second beat of clarification, suggesting the initial legitimacy framing landed thin for someone who wasn't expecting the call.

Rather than reflecting back what the rep already heard (a 'free solar' expectation) to keep control of the frame, the rep asks an open question that lets the customer restate and escalate her frustration before the rep responds.

key_moments.quote: Solar is just a scam, but I appreciate your call.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer explicitly frames the experience as a scam after the free-solar expectation wasn't met. No script-defined rebuttal in Ion's current schema maps cleanly to this marketing-expectation-gap version of the trust objection — the closest schema entry (how_did_you_get_my_number) addresses a different concern (how contact info was obtained), not this one.

key_moments.quote: We don't have free solar. We have a no upfront, no out of pocket cost solar, but it's not free. You'd still have to pay for the equipment.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is not actually a knowledge gap in the negative sense — the rep gives an accurate, honest correction of the marketing claim rather than fabricating a 'free solar' story to keep the call alive. This protects trust even though it doesn't recover the sale.
